answer: To curb Sybil attacks, an agent economy can harbor graph-theoretic trust networks that restrict peer admission at each network inlet. Nodes verify prospective peers by calculating bounded random walks rooted at trusted bootstrap seeds. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of establishing scarce, authentic trust edges across the network cut, dispelling the fable of costless agent replication. However, this approach creates an acute cold-start penalty for legitimate newcomer agents.
